newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber down on back of Japanese holiday.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber down on back of Japanese holiday.

text.p: Rubber futures closed mostly marginally lower on Monday on the back of weak sentiment caused by a holiday in Japan, dealers said.

"Everything was practically dead. The holiday in Japan drove players in the market to the sidelines. They would prefer to wait for Japan to reopen tomorrow and see where prices would head," a local rubber trader said.
Dealers said there was some light buying for RSS3 rubber, but activity in other brands remained lacklustre.
One dealer said: "The mood in the market was very quiet and dull. Almost no deals were done. It became a waiting game."
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 128.50-129.00 U.S. cents a kg from 129.25 cents.
November RSS1 was seen around 185.00-186.00 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.32) a kg from Friday's settlement of 185.50 cents.
November TSR20 was seen at 179.00-180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from 180.00 cents.
